records.title_fr: Règlement sur les animaux domestiques et les chiens dangereux
records.fines: $300–$2,000 individual · $500–$4,000 company (art. 66); each day is a separate offence (art. 67)
key_facts_en: Dogs are placed in the "at-risk", "potentially dangerous" or "dangerous" categories according to a bite, an attack or other conduct, or a declaration by the competent authority (art. 4, 44 to 47).
A dog or cat licence is valid for the life of the animal (art. 20, 25).
In the urban perimeter, keeping hens may be permitted: at most 5 hens, no rooster, and one coop per lot in the side or rear yard, subject to the zoning bylaw (art. 12).
Fines range from $300 to $4,000 (art. 66). Costs incurred in applying the bylaw to an animal, such as capture, boarding and veterinary care, are charged to its keeper (art. 9).

records.fines: $10,000–$250,000 for demolishing without approval; up to $1,140,000 for a company demolishing a cited heritage building (art. 2.6); obstruction $300–$1,000 (art. 2.7)
key_facts_en: Demolishing a building, in whole or in part, is prohibited unless the owner has been authorized under the bylaw and the municipality has issued a demolition certificate; the certificate follows an authorization by the demolition committee or by council (art. 4.1–4.2). Under the bylaw, moving a building also counts as demolition (art. 1.10).

The committee is three council members designated by council resolution for one year, plus a substitute (art. 3.1). Council designated the current members and substitute by resolution 26-06-172 of June 1, 2026. The bylaw says the committee is decision-making (décisionnel) and its sittings are public (art. 3.2).

Once an application is complete, a notice is posted on the building and published as a public notice. Anyone may file a written, reasoned objection with the municipal clerk within 10 days (art. 4.9, 4.11).
Anyone may ask council to review the committee's decision within 30 days, and no certificate can be issued before that period ends (art. 4.18, 4.24).
Demolishing a principal building without authorization carries a fine of $10,000 to $250,000, and the offender must rebuild what was demolished (art. 2.6, 2.8).
Annex A, the inventory of heritage buildings the bylaw refers to, consists of one line: “(en attente de la MRC du Haut-Saint-Laurent)” (awaiting the MRC du Haut-Saint-Laurent).

records.title_fr: Règlement concernant le Plan d'Urbanisme 147-2023
Règlement de zonage
key_facts_en: No one may fell a tree of 3 cm in diameter or more, measured 30 cm from the ground, without first obtaining a certificat d'autorisation d'abattage d'arbres (zoning art. 12.8). Bylaw 39-2026 sets the fee at $25 for a residential certificate ($50 for more than 4 trees) and $50 for others ($75 for more than 4 trees).

Inside the urban perimeter, every lot must keep at least one tree per 100 m² of land area. If trees felled for a reason listed in article 12.10 bring a lot below that density, they must be replaced, outside agricultural zones, with species from an approved list (art. 12.5).

Felling a tree of 30 cm in diameter in contravention of the bylaw carries a fine of at least $500 plus $100 to $200 per tree, or $5,000 to $15,000 per full hectare for clearing of a hectare or more; the amounts are doubled on a repeat offence (art. 2.9).

The zoning bylaw requires the certificate for a tree of 3 cm or more (art. 12.8); the permits bylaw requires it for a tree whose diameter is greater than 0.1 metre (art. 3.15). Both measure 30 cm from the ground.
The copy of 148-2023 posted on ormstown.ca lists no amendments. According to the town's notices, Bylaw 148.4-2025, adopted April 13, 2026, amends provisions on shorelines, littoral and flood zones.

records.title_en: Plan of Implantation and Architectural Integration (PIIA)
records.title_fr: Plan d'implantation et d'intégration architecturale (PIIA)
key_facts_en: For the work the bylaw lists, a building permit or certificate is issued only after council approves the PIIA by resolution, taking into account the recommendation of the advisory planning committee (CCU) (art. 3.7–3.9).

It applies in the architectural core, in the Route 201 Sud and C-7 sector, in zone R-37 (rue Isabelle), and, anywhere in the municipality, to the construction of any detached accessory dwelling unit (UHAD) (art. 1.7).
In the architectural core, painting that changes the colour of the principal building needs approval; a change within the same tones, such as white to cream white, does not (art. 4.2).
Fines, for each day or part of a day: $500 to $1,000 for an individual and $600 to $2,000 for a legal person on a first offence; $800 to $2,000 and $800 to $4,000 on a repeat offence (art. 2.7).

records.title_en: Rules of Procedure for Council Meetings
records.title_fr: Règlement de procédure du conseil municipal
key_facts_en: Règlement 2-2026 came into force on April 17, 2026. It replaces and repeals any earlier municipal bylaw adopted on the same subject (art. 52).

Every ordinary meeting has two public question periods of up to 30 minutes each, one before the meeting opens and one after it closes. Each person has up to 5 minutes to ask a question and receive the answer (art. 33.1, 35).

A meeting ends 3 hours after it begins. Unfinished business resumes at 6:30 p.m. the next juridical day, unless two-thirds of the members present vote to adjourn or suspend for a shorter period (art. 17).

The mayor may refuse to approve a council decision by notifying the clerk in writing within 48 hours; council may lift this suspensive veto by re-adopting the resolution by an absolute majority of its members (art. 41.1).

Article 3 says ordinary meetings are usually held on the "premier lundi mercredi" of each month, and that council fixes the annual calendar of ordinary meetings by resolution. The municipality's 2026 calendar notice sets all twelve 2026 ordinary meetings on Mondays.

Code d'éthique et de déontologie des employés municipaux de la Municipalité d'Ormstown
key_facts_en: Employees may not accept any gift, hospitality or other benefit offered by a supplier (art. 7.3.5).
A possible conflict of interest must be reported to the immediate supervisor (art. 7.4).
Staff need the director general's prior authorization to publish a text or give an interview about their duties or the municipality's activities (art. 12).
Staff involved in tenders or contracts face a one-year limit on working for a municipal bidder or supplier after leaving (art. 7.4).
Sanctions range from a verbal notice to dismissal (art. 13.2).

records.title_fr: Règlement 86-2024 – Utilisation de l'eau potable
key_facts_en: Lawn watering is permitted only from 3 to 6 a.m. with an automatic system and only from 8 to 11 p.m. with a mechanical system, on one weekday set by the last digit of the address (art. 7.3). Article 7.3 lists no Saturday or Sunday.
Manual watering of a garden, vegetable plot, flower box, planter, flower bed, tree or shrub is permitted at any time (art. 7.2).
Article 7.9 lists the terms for filling a pool: between May 1 and June 15; on an even date for an even civic number and an odd date for an odd one; at any time after June 15.

Air conditioning, refrigeration systems and compressors that use drinking water, and automatic-flush urinals with a purge tank, installed before the bylaw came into force must be replaced before February 1, 2027 (art. 6.2, 6.8). Automatic car washes must have a water recovery and recycling system before the same date (art. 7.11).
Fines run $250–$500 for a first offence by an individual and up to $3,000 for a further repeat offence by a corporation, plus administration fees (art. 8.4).
